# Expert knowledge: the research behind the skill pack

This folder holds the research every skill in the pack stands on. Each topic folder has a `README.md` (the
findings, in plain words), an `evidence.md` (every claim with its source and its strength) and a `sources.md`
(every link, and whether it was read in full or only in summary).
`claude-setup/` has no `evidence.md` because its facts are Anthropic's own pages.

All of it was written or re-checked on 2026-10-29 (icp/ on 2026-10-30). Research round 2 (2026-10-30) added
`practitioners/` and dated "Round 2" notes in the topic folders; its tests and decisions are `method/README.md`
section 7. Read the topic README before changing the skill that relies on it.

## How strong is the evidence

The folders use close cousins of one scale. From strongest to weakest:

| Level | Means |
|---|---|
| Official / DOC | A platform, a mailbox provider, a regulator or Anthropic says it. A rule, not a result |
| Measured / DATA | A study or meta-analysis with a stated method and sample, not run by someone selling the thing measured |
| Measured (vendor) | A seller's own dataset with a stated sample. Observational: trust the direction, not the size |
| Survey | People asked about themselves |
| Practice | A named practitioner's method. Nobody measured it |
| LOCAL | Measured inside BeReach on its own customers |
| Untraced / FOLKLORE | Repeated everywhere, no source found |

One rule runs through every folder: almost nothing about outreach has been tested in a controlled way. Most
numbers are vendor correlations. The only number about a user's own messages is their own, read in
`bereach_status` (`connections.trend`).

## The index

| Topic folder | What it covers | The 3 most useful findings | Strongest evidence | Where it is used |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`method/`](method/README.md) | The outreach loop (ICP, persona, voice, one template with each brief's personal line, measure) and how to measure it honestly with small numbers | 1. Compare cohorts at the same age: 88% of acceptances arrive within 7 days, so a raw weekly rate always makes this week look worse. 2. At LinkedIn volumes only big changes can be proven: 30% to 40% acceptance needs about 360 people per arm; under 100 per arm gives a direction, never a verdict. 3. Peeking and stopping at the first "significant" gap gave 26% false wins instead of 5% (Evan Miller); fix the size before looking | DATA (standard experiment statistics, Kohavi et al., Miller) plus LOCAL | linkedin-outreach-method |
| [`personas/`](personas/README.md) | What separates an ICP from a persona, what a persona card holds, how to put each lead in one persona | 1. ICP picks the companies, persona picks the people and what to say: two stages, in order (Wind and Cardozo 1974). 2. A persona is a role in a situation, not a person with a life; keep it short and label it a guess until replies confirm it (Goodwin's provisional persona; at 9+ attributes a description matches almost nobody, Chapman 2008). 3. The title selects a card, it is never the content of the message; write to the role's problem (Revella's 5 rings, the four forces of Moesta and Spiek, Gartner 2025 on group-level relevance) | Measured, but indirect (Chapman 2008; CEB and Gartner surveys). No study measures persona cards on reply rates | linkedin-personas |
| [`icp/`](icp/README.md) | What an ICP is for search and where it stops: the layers (market, segment, ICP, buying group, buying role, persona, qualification), which fields earn their place, the frameworks and their authors, and the words the pack uses for each | 1. An ICP is the company half of a plan segment; a plan group is the searchable half of a persona; fit decides who is in, timing decides the order. 2. Every field narrows geometrically: at 9+ attributes the best 1% of descriptions matched nobody in 5 of 6 datasets (Chapman 2008), so read the whole plan's count. 3. Ask who decides, never infer it: a firm's facts predicted its buying group 47% of the time against 27% chance (Choffray and Lilien 1980); no outbound list, broad or narrow, has ever been measured | Measured, indirect (Chapman 2008, Choffray and Lilien 1980, Mora Cortez 2021); most frameworks are untested Practice | linkedin-outreach-method, linkedin-personas |
| [`voice/`](voice/README.md) | How to capture the way one person writes and check a draft against it | 1. 3 to 5 real messages are enough; going from 2 to 10 samples changed results very little (Wang et al. 2025, 400+ authors, six models). 2. Choose samples for variety: picking them on the target's topic dropped the match from 95.4% to 81.3%. 3. Check a draft by counting (length, sentence length, punctuation, greeting, sign-off, address form), never by asking a model: a model judge called two drafts of the same prompt different in 70 of 72 pairs | DATA (Wang et al. 2025, EMNLP Findings) plus LOCAL | linkedin-voice |
| [`linkedin-messages/`](linkedin-messages/README.md) | The invitation note, the first message after acceptance, follow-ups and the five-message sequence; the named experts; fake personalization | 1. The customer's failure has a name: a recited fact (a title, a headline) with no "so what". The personal line is one sentence with a verb that ties a fact to the reason for writing. 2. Ask for interest or offer something, never a meeting first (meeting ask -44%, offer +28%, 85M emails). 3. A note is a filter, not a lever: acceptance 0 to 5 points lower with a note, replies higher; write to 200 characters, 3 notes a month on a free account | Measured, peer reviewed for the mechanism (Sahni et al. 2018, Jakesch et al. 2019); the rest vendor data with stated samples | linkedin-messages |
| [`linkedin-channel/`](linkedin-channel/README.md) | LinkedIn itself as a channel: the platform's rules, its own published data, acceptance and reply benchmarks, profile, warm-up, voice and video, timing, length, follow-up count | 1. A passive warm-up (a view, a like) does not raise acceptance and may lower it (Waalaxy, 21M requests: 32.9% with a visit, 34.2% without); a real tie the person knows about (they followed you, a shared group or colleague) does. 2. Sane baselines: acceptance 20% to 30%, under 13% means the list or profile is wrong; about 18% of accepted people reply, under 10% means the message is wrong. 3. Two or three messages after acceptance over two to six weeks, then stop; day and hour barely move replies | Measured (one): the LinkedOut field experiment (QJE 2025, about 20,000 requests). The rest vendor, with two randomized vendor tests | linkedin-messages, linkedin-outreach-method |
| [`outreach-frameworks/`](outreach-frameworks/README.md) | Sales frameworks that shape a first message and a sequence: SPIN, Challenger, Sandler, Gap Selling, NEPQ, ValueSelling, Command of the Message, Braun, McKenna, Bay, 30MPC, Lavender, Holland, signal selling, social selling, cadences, the breakup | 1. Every framework with data behind it agrees: talk about their problem, not your product (Rackham's observed calls; pitching cut replies up to 57% in the 85M emails). 2. The reason to write is the strongest line, and a dated event or their own activity is the strongest reason (activity-based 24% reply against 2% for none). 3. The famous frameworks are meeting frameworks; a first DM that runs a full SPIN or pain funnel is an interrogation by text. Keep one question type, the problem-first stance, and no commitment ask | Measured (vendor, observational: 85M emails, Gong 304K emails); Rackham's 35,000 observed calls (author's own firm) | linkedin-messages, linkedin-outreach-method, cold-email |
| [`copy-frameworks/`](copy-frameworks/README.md) | Every copywriting framework a note, a DM or a cold email can borrow (AIDA, PAS, BAB, FAB, 4Ps, 4Us, QUEST, Star-Story-Solution, Schwartz, Caples, Ogilvy), traced to its author, with a decision table by message type and awareness | 1. The order of the parts is not what persuades, the parts are: the one controlled test of an order found no difference, and hierarchy models have little support (Vakratsas and Ambler, 250+ papers). Never claim one framework "converts better". 2. What persuades, over 1,149 studies: more evidence (r = .225), showing the fix works and is easy (about r = .20), explicit over implicit arguments (r = .138); gain or loss framing does nothing (r = .016). So "agitate" is the weakest part of PAS. 3. A cold B2B reader cannot be sold in the first line, only identified (Schwartz, read in his own text); specific beats general (Caples, Ogilvy, lab work on precise numbers) | Measured meta-analysis (O'Keefe and Hoeken 2021, 1,149 studies, about 280,000 people) | linkedin-messages, cold-email |
| [`behavioural-science/`](behavioural-science/README.md) | The persuasion effects outreach advice leans on (Cialdini's six and a handful of named studies), each with its replication record | 1. Published effect sizes are inflated: nudge units averaged 1.4 points against 8.7 points in journals (DellaVigna and Linos 2022). Expect a few percent from any trick, or nothing. 2. What holds: reciprocity (give something useful first; up-front incentives beat promised ones, OR 1.61, Cochrane, 481 trials), specificity, and a real reason (a real "because" nearly doubled compliance on a large favour, an empty one did nothing). 3. What failed or is weak: "but you are free" (no effect in low-bias studies), scarcity, door in the face, curiosity teases, loss framing, the first name as a lever. The AI penalty falls on generic text, not on the tool | Measured: meta-analyses, a Cochrane review and preregistered replications | linkedin-messages, cold-email |
| [`french-market/`](french-market/README.md) | Writing to French-speaking B2B readers in France, Belgium, Switzerland and Quebec: vous or tu by sector, length, tone, buyer studies, LinkedIn figures, each regulator's rules, good and bad examples | 1. No published test compares tu and vous on B2B replies in any French-speaking market: default vous with the first name, mirror the reader once they write tu (consumer experiments put an expert seller in the "competent", formal case). 2. Every French first message carries who writes, why this reader in terms of their job, where the contact came from, and an easy no: the CNIL conditions and good copy at once. 3. French buyers research alone for about 12 months before the first sales contact (Infopro, 205 decision makers): offer a useful angle, not a product tour; one clause of reason before the ask | Official (CNIL, the KASPR decision, Canada's CRTC); the buyer data is Survey | linkedin-messages, linkedin-voice, linkedin-personas, cold-email |
| [`cold-email/`](cold-email/README.md) | Cold email: mailbox provider rules, the law (CAN-SPAM, GDPR, CNIL, UK, Germany), writing frameworks, length, subject, personalization, CTA, tracking, sequences, volume, warm-up, timing, French senders | 1. The rules that bite at any volume: SPF and DKIM (and DMARC), spam complaints under 0.1% and never 0.3% (Google), no hard bounces. 2. Interest asks win: a meeting followed 30% of the time after "worth exploring?" against 15% after a specific time ask (Gong, 304K emails); tracking off replied 7.4% against 4.4% on (Hunter, 31M). 3. 3 to 4 emails over two to three weeks, each adding something new; 50 to 90 words for the first. "80% of sales need five follow-ups" traces to nothing | Official (Google, Yahoo, Microsoft, FTC, CNIL, EDPB) | cold-email |
| [`practitioners/`](practitioners/README.md) | Round 2 (2026-10-30): Pierre Herubel and 17 recognised experts or datasets the pack covered thinly, each with a verdict: taken, already in, or rejected | 1. Herubel is a content creator ("outbound is not my specialty"): his useful ideas are warm, signal-led outbound, the topic as the angle, ask before sending, one offer, specific follow-ups; most were already in the pack. 2. Four small changes passed a blind test (gaps +1.83 to +3.83); three are in the pack: a named colleague gets a referral first message, a deferral is not a yes (Mom Test), AI tells counted after drafting (Russell 2025); a comment on the user's own post first was reverted after a re-test. 3. Rejected: directness by signal strength, weekly nurture, Voss labels, priming, word or grade targets, the 15-touch sequence | Measured (Russell 2025, Yeomans 2020); Measured (vendor, randomized: Prospectio shared colleague); the rest Practice or vendor | linkedin-messages, linkedin-voice, linkedin-outreach-method |
| [`claude-setup/`](claude-setup/README.md) | Where Claude is steered (profile instructions, memory, projects, skills, connectors, artifacts), how to install the pack, and why piled-up memory makes output worse | 1. Contradicting instructions are resolved at random, and longer instruction files lower adherence (Anthropic's own docs; at 500 instructions the best models followed 68%, IFScale 2025). 2. Outreach rules belong in one reviewed place: the skills plus one playbook saved in BeReach; tone rules in memory or project instructions are an unreviewed second copy that drifts. 3. Upload a skill at Customize > Skills (one ZIP per skill, description under 200 characters); BeReach itself is set up by giving the agent one line, `set up bereach - https://bereach.ai/llms.txt`; deleting a chat does not delete what memory learned from it | DOC (Anthropic documentation, read 2026-10-29) plus DATA (IFScale, ConInstruct) | bereach-setup |

## What every folder agrees on

- **Relevance does the work, tricks adjust.** A real reason tied to the reader's role or recent activity is the
  strongest lever in every source: the 85M email data, Schwartz, Holland, the replication record, the CNIL's
  own condition. No sentence trick rescues a message sent to the wrong person.
- **Problem before product, interest before meeting, an easy no.** Measured in email, practiced by every named
  expert, and the honest default on LinkedIn.
- **Short, specific, plain.** 2 to 4 sentences, about 150 to 400 characters for a first LinkedIn message, one
  checkable fact, no buzzwords.
- **Measure your own.** Vendor benchmarks are for sanity, never for promises. Same persona, same week, random
  split, read at 7 days, no verdict under 100 per arm.

## Gaps nobody has filled

No controlled test anywhere of: one copy framework against another; tu against vous; persona cards against no
cards; a headline, banner or "About" section on acceptance; voice notes outside one founder-led segment.
Each is a test BeReach can run on a user's own numbers with `bereach_connect` and `bereach_status`.

## Note on links to the skills

The pack's top `README.md` links to some of these folders by path. The skills themselves carry the rules
in their own reference files (frameworks, first message, legal, persona and voice cards) without a path link. The "where it is used" column names the skill whose rules come from each folder.
